Severity assessment: medium is correct. The reviewer's own notes explicitly document that duckdb_result (48B), enum values (VARINT/BIGNUM=35, TIME_NS=39), and all other struct layouts are stable across the supported 1.3.2-1.5 range. The practical blast radius within that range is limited — a Homebrew/pip version skew within 1.3-1.5 is unlikely to corrupt data because the C API ABI is stable. However, the defect is real: (a) no version check means a skew outside the stable window (e.g., Homebrew advances beyond 1.5 while pip stays pinned) silently loads a mismatched runtime with no diagnostic; (b) no logging of which native library/version was actually loaded makes debugging silent failures impossible. Medium is the right severity — the issue is genuine and the fix is low-cost (bind duckdb_library_version and compare), but it is not high because struct/enum stability limits the practical risk within the declared supported range.
